nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong desert sun drives growth, but it also bakes the ground; shade under trees keeps young cacti alive.

nodes.name: Winter and monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Two rainy seasons feed the desert, and water is one of the main reasons it holds so many species. Washes run only after storms and can flash flood.

nodes.name: Desert soil
nodes.desc: Thin, dry soil whose nutrients return mainly through decay and the shade and litter under trees such as palo verde.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals, including fallen saguaros, and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Saguaro
nodes.desc: The park's namesake giant cactus. It stores rainwater, flowers feed bats, bees and birds, and its fruit feeds doves; woodpecker holes become homes for other birds.

nodes.name: Foothill palo verde
nodes.desc: A green-barked desert tree that acts as a nurse plant, shading young saguaros and softening temperature extremes around them.

nodes.name: Velvet mesquite
nodes.desc: A desert tree whose seed pods and foliage feed many animals.

nodes.name: Engelmann prickly pear
nodes.desc: A pad-forming cactus whose pads and fruit are food for javelinas, rabbits and other desert animals.

nodes.name: White-winged dove
nodes.desc: Eats saguaro fruit and seeds, and also pollinates saguaro flowers. Wikipedia says saguaro can make up most of its diet in the season.

nodes.name: Gila woodpecker
nodes.desc: Digs a new nest hole in saguaros each season; abandoned holes shelter elf owls, flycatchers and other birds.

nodes.name: Western honey bee
nodes.desc: Wikipedia lists honey bees among the main pollinators of saguaro, visiting its flowers for nectar.

nodes.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
nodes.desc: A large hare that grazes grasses and browses shrubs and cacti; prey for many desert predators.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: Also called javelina. Eats prickly pear pads and mesquite pods and travels in herds.

nodes.name: Merriam's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: A small seed-eating rodent of desert flats that does not need to drink; a main prey for snakes and owls.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: The park's larger browser, taking leaves and twigs of desert shrubs and trees.

nodes.name: Western diamondback rattlesnake
nodes.desc: An ambush predator of rodents, rabbits and birds.

nodes.name: Gila monster
nodes.desc: A slow venomous lizard that raids burrows and nests for eggs and small animals.

nodes.name: Gray fox
nodes.desc: An omnivorous canid that hunts rodents and rabbits and eats fruit.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A scavenger that feeds on carrion such as animals killed on park roads.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A widespread predator and scavenger, taking rabbits, rodents, deer and carrion.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A solitary cat that hunts rabbits, rodents, birds and sometimes deer.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A soaring hawk that preys on rabbits, rodents, birds and snakes.
